title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: SharePoint list as a knowledge source in Agent Builder
summary: The briefing passes. Microsoft's documentation supports the list limits, licensing alternatives and agent-blocking controls, and the rollout facts match the roadmap. The open questions are narrowly framed around details not found in the documentation.

claims.claim: Agent Builder supports a SharePoint list as agent knowledge.
claims.quote: Reference specific files, folders, lists, and sites as agent knowledge sources.

claims.claim: An agent can answer questions using structured information in the selected list.
claims.quote: Makers can ground an agent in structured list data so users can ask questions and get responses based on information stored in a selected SharePoint list.

claims.claim: Each agent can reference one SharePoint list.

claims.quote: For this release, each agent can reference one SharePoint list with up to 20,000 items, alongside other knowledge source types.

claims.claim: The admin route to block an agent is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. ... In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents. ... In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks the selected Copilot package.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: User access is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access.

claims.claim: All users is the default User access option.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.claim: User access offers a No users option.
claims.quote:
No users - This option means that no users in the organization can access agents and plugins.
Specific users or groups - This option lets you select specific users or groups in your organization to have access to agents and plugins.

claims.claim: User access governs agent and plugin access, not Agent Builder creation independently.

claims.claim: Sharing-setting changes apply only to new sharing actions.
